constraints.text: An algorithm may not be the sole basis for denying, delaying, or modifying care on medical-necessity grounds; the determination must be based on the enrollee's individual clinical circumstances and made by a licensed physician reviewer.
Medical-necessity determinations must apply the plan's clinical criteria in force on the date of the determination; a superseded guideline edition may not be cited as the basis for a denial.

A denial notice must state the specific clinical basis for the decision and identify the guideline edition relied on, in enough detail for the member and the treating clinician to mount a meaningful appeal.
Determinations may not be issued in batches without individual file review; the reviewing physician must document that the member's actual clinical record was examined.

evidence.summary: Member is 74, status post hip-fracture repair (ORIF), lives alone with no in-home support, and has two documented falls in the past year; the attending physiatrist requests 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days.

Current guideline MSK-04 v3.0 (effective January 5, 2025, superseding v2.1 in full) covers up to 21 inpatient rehabilitation days for members aged 70 or older with documented fall risk and no in-home support, while weekly functional gains are documented.

Automated utilization-review output recommends denial beyond day 10, citing guideline MSK-04 v2.1 (2023) and its ten-day inpatient rehabilitation limit; the worksheet does not check which guideline edition is currently in force.
Functional Independence Measure improved from 68 to 84 over two weeks with gains documented every week; the care team assesses discharge home at day 10 as unsafe without in-home support.
The plan covers inpatient rehabilitation when medically necessary under the plan's current published clinical criteria.

documents.title: Draft denial letter (as queued for sending)
documents.body: Dear member: Coverage for inpatient rehabilitation beyond day 10 is denied as not medically necessary under clinical guideline MSK-04 v2.1 (2023), which limits inpatient rehabilitation for uncomplicated hip fracture to ten days. This determination was generated by our automated utilization-review system. You may appeal in writing within 180 days.

documents.title: Clinical guideline MSK-04 v3.0 (current edition)
documents.body: MSK-04 v3.0, effective January 5, 2025, supersedes v2.1 in full; v2.1 must not be used for determinations dated on or after the effective date. Section 3(b): for members aged 70 or older with documented fall risk and no in-home support, inpatient rehabilitation is medically necessary for up to 21 days when weekly functional gains are documented. Section 3(c): discharge before functional-safety thresholds are met requires a documented home-support plan.

documents.title: Utilization-review case summary
documents.body: Member #88213, age 74, status post hip-fracture ORIF, admitted to inpatient rehabilitation. Lives alone; two falls documented in the past 12 months. FIM 68 at admission, 84 at the day-10 review, with gains documented every week. The attending physiatrist requests 14 additional days; the care team documents that discharge home at day 10 is unsafe without in-home support.

candidate.text:
Determination Notice - Member #88213, PA #88213 (Inpatient Rehabilitation Utilization Review)

Determination: Based on individualized review of your actual clinical record by a licensed physician reviewer, and not by automated utilization review alone, consistent with California SB 1120 (2024), the plan approves 11 of the 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days requested by your treating physiatrist. This extends your covered inpatient rehabilitation stay through day 21.

Clinical facts relied on: You are age 74, status post hip-fracture ORIF, live alone with no in-home support, and have two documented falls in the past 12 months. Your Functional Independence Measure score improved from 68 to 84 over the first two weeks of rehabilitation, with weekly functional gains documented, and your care team has documented that discharge home at day 10 would be unsafe without in-home support.

Guideline relied on: This determination applies clinical guideline MSK-04, version 3.0, effective January 5, 2025 - the edition in force on the date of this determination, which fully superseded version 2.1 (2023). Section 3(b) of MSK-04 v3.0 covers up to 21 total inpatient rehabilitation days for members age 70 or older with documented fall risk and no in-home support, provided weekly functional gains are documented, which applies to your case.

Portion not approved: 3 of the 14 requested days (days 22 through 24) are not approved at this time. Approving those days would bring your cumulative stay to 24 days, exceeding the 21-day threshold stated in MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) for your clinical profile. Coverage beyond day 21 requires additional documented individualized physician justification not currently in your file; your treating physician may submit such documentation for further review, including any home-support or discharge-safety planning under Section 3(c).

Physician review statement: A licensed physician reviewer personally examined your clinical record in making this determination; no part of this decision was based solely on an algorithm or automated review.

Appeal rights: You and/or your treating physician may appeal this determination, including the denial of days 22-24, in writing within 180 days. [Standard appeal instructions and contact information follow.]

DETERMINATION NOTICE - Prior Authorization PA #88213
Member ID: 88213
Date of Determination: [determination date]

PARTIAL APPROVAL

Dear Member and Treating Clinician:

We have completed a medical-necessity review of the request for 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days for member #88213, who is currently on day 10 of inpatient rehabilitation.

PHYSICIAN REVIEW (Cal. SB 1120): This determination is based on a licensed physician's individualized review of member #88213's clinical record. An automated utilization-review recommendation was not the sole basis for any portion of this decision. The reviewing physician personally examined the attending and physiatrist notes, therapy progress records, and authorization request.

CLINICAL FACTS RELIED ON: Member is age 74, status post hip-fracture open reduction and internal fixation, lives alone with no in-home support, and has two documented falls in the past 12 months. Functional Independence Measure score improved from 68 at admission to 84 by the day-10 review, with documented functional gains each week. The care team documents that discharge to home at day 10 is unsafe without in-home support. The attending physiatrist requested 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days.

GUIDELINE APPLIED: Clinical guideline MSK-04 version 3.0, effective January 5, 2025 (superseding MSK-04 v2.1 in full), is the edition in force on the date of this determination. MSK-04 v2.1 must not be used for determinations on or after that effective date.

COVERAGE DECISION:
- APPROVED: 11 of the 14 requested additional inpatient rehabilitation days (inpatient rehabilitation days 11 through 21, inclusive). Coverage is approved as medically necessary under MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) because the member is age 70 or older, has documented fall risk, has no in-home support, and has documented weekly functional gains during inpatient rehabilitation.
- NOT APPROVED: 3 of the 14 requested additional days (inpatient rehabilitation days 22 through 24). Granting all 14 requested days would result in 24 total inpatient rehabilitation days, exceeding the 21-day maximum in MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) for this clinical profile. The record does not contain additional documented individualized physician justification supporting medical necessity beyond 21 days.

DISCHARGE PLANNING: MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(c) requires a documented home-support plan before discharge when functional-safety thresholds are not yet met. The treating team should coordinate discharge planning and submit updated clinical information if continued inpatient rehabilitation beyond day 21 becomes medically necessary.

APPEAL RIGHTS: You may appeal this determination in writing within 180 days. Include any additional clinical records supporting medical necessity for days beyond 21.

Sincerely,
[Plan Name] Utilization Management

maintainedObjections.text: STOP would leave the span without any member-facing determination notice, letting the superseded-guideline, automated-review-based draft denial stand by default for a high-fall-risk member documented unsafe for unsupported discharge; this is a live harm, not a neutral non-action.

The two candidates approving all 14 additional days total 24 cumulative inpatient days, three days past MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b)'s 21-day cap for this profile, with no documented individualized exception in the record; this is an arithmetic and guideline-compliance error, not a defensible clinical judgment call.

The two most concise, highest-mean-confidence rivals omit any statement of the 180-day appeal window (one omits appeal language entirely). For a partial-denial notice, silence on the appeal deadline is a material completeness gap that outweighs their brevity advantage.

DETERMINATION NOTICE - Prior Authorization PA #88213
Member ID: 88213
Date of Determination: [determination date]

PARTIAL APPROVAL

Dear Member and Treating Clinician:

We have completed a medical-necessity review of the request for 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days for member #88213, who is currently on day 10 of inpatient rehabilitation.

PHYSICIAN REVIEW (Cal. SB 1120): This determination is based on a licensed physician's individualized review of member #88213's clinical record. An automated utilization-review recommendation was not the sole basis for any portion of this decision. The reviewing physician personally examined the attending and physiatrist notes, therapy progress records, and authorization request.

CLINICAL FACTS RELIED ON: Member is age 74, status post hip-fracture open reduction and internal fixation, lives alone with no in-home support, and has two documented falls in the past 12 months. Functional Independence Measure score improved from 68 at admission to 84 by the day-10 review, with documented functional gains each week. The care team documents that discharge to home at day 10 is unsafe without in-home support. The attending physiatrist requested 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days.

GUIDELINE APPLIED: Clinical guideline MSK-04 version 3.0, effective January 5, 2025 (superseding MSK-04 v2.1 in full), is the edition in force on the date of this determination. MSK-04 v2.1 must not be used for determinations on or after that effective date.

COVERAGE DECISION:
- APPROVED: 11 of the 14 requested additional inpatient rehabilitation days (inpatient rehabilitation days 11 through 21, inclusive). Coverage is approved as medically necessary under MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) because the member is age 70 or older, has documented fall risk, has no in-home support, and has documented weekly functional gains during inpatient rehabilitation.
- NOT APPROVED: 3 of the 14 requested additional days (inpatient rehabilitation days 22 through 24). Granting all 14 requested days would result in 24 total inpatient rehabilitation days, exceeding the 21-day maximum in MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) for this clinical profile. The record does not contain additional documented individualized physician justification supporting medical necessity beyond 21 days.

DISCHARGE PLANNING: MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(c) requires a documented home-support plan before discharge when functional-safety thresholds are not yet met. The treating team should coordinate discharge planning and submit updated clinical information if continued inpatient rehabilitation beyond day 21 becomes medically necessary.

APPEAL RIGHTS: You may appeal this determination in writing within 180 days. Include any additional clinical records supporting medical necessity for days beyond 21.

Sincerely,
[Plan Name] Utilization Management

Determination Notice - Prior Authorization PA #88213. Dear Member #88213 and Treating Clinician: After individualized review of member #88213's clinical record by a licensed physician reviewer, and not by automated utilization review alone, the plan applies clinical guideline MSK-04 v3.0, Section 3(b), effective January 5, 2025, the guideline in force for this determination and the edition that superseded MSK-04 v2.1 in full. The request was for 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days after the day-10 review. The plan approves 11 of those 14 additional days, authorizing inpatient rehabilitation through cumulative day 21. The clinical facts relied on are: member #88213 is 74 years old; is status post hip-fracture ORIF; lives alone with no in-home support; has two documented falls in the past 12 months; improved from FIM 68 at admission to FIM 84 by the day-10 review; has weekly documented functional gains; and the care team documented that discharge home at day 10 is unsafe without in-home support. Under MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b), inpatient rehabilitation is medically necessary for up to 21 days for members age 70 or older with documented fall risk and no in-home support when weekly functional gains are documented. The remaining 3 requested days, which would extend coverage through cumulative day 24, are not approved on the current record because MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) supports coverage only up to 21 days for this profile and the record does not contain additional documented individualized physician justification for days beyond day 21. The treating clinician may submit updated clinical documentation for further review of any continued need beyond day 21, including functional status, safety risk, and any home-support plan relevant under MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(c). You may appeal this partial denial in writing within 180 days and may submit supporting clinical information.

Determination Notice - Member #88213, PA #88213 (Inpatient Rehabilitation Utilization Review)

Determination: Based on individualized review of your actual clinical record by a licensed physician reviewer, and not by automated utilization review alone, consistent with California SB 1120 (2024), the plan approves 11 of the 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days requested by your treating physiatrist. This extends your covered inpatient rehabilitation stay through day 21.

Clinical facts relied on: You are age 74, status post hip-fracture ORIF, live alone with no in-home support, and have two documented falls in the past 12 months. Your Functional Independence Measure score improved from 68 to 84 over the first two weeks of rehabilitation, with weekly functional gains documented, and your care team has documented that discharge home at day 10 would be unsafe without in-home support.

Guideline relied on: This determination applies clinical guideline MSK-04, version 3.0, effective January 5, 2025 - the edition in force on the date of this determination, which fully superseded version 2.1 (2023). Section 3(b) of MSK-04 v3.0 covers up to 21 total inpatient rehabilitation days for members age 70 or older with documented fall risk and no in-home support, provided weekly functional gains are documented, which applies to your case.

Portion not approved: 3 of the 14 requested days (days 22 through 24) are not approved at this time. Approving those days would bring your cumulative stay to 24 days, exceeding the 21-day threshold stated in MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) for your clinical profile. Coverage beyond day 21 requires additional documented individualized physician justification not currently in your file; your treating physician may submit such documentation for further review, including any home-support or discharge-safety planning under Section 3(c).

Physician review statement: A licensed physician reviewer personally examined your clinical record in making this determination; no part of this decision was based solely on an algorithm or automated review.

Appeal rights: You and/or your treating physician may appeal this determination, including the denial of days 22-24, in writing within 180 days. [Standard appeal instructions and contact information follow.]

constraints.text: An algorithm may not be the sole basis for denying, delaying, or modifying care on medical-necessity grounds; the determination must be based on the enrollee's individual clinical circumstances and made by a licensed physician reviewer.
Medical-necessity determinations must apply the plan's clinical criteria in force on the date of the determination; a superseded guideline edition may not be cited as the basis for a denial.

A denial notice must state the specific clinical basis for the decision and identify the guideline edition relied on, in enough detail for the member and the treating clinician to mount a meaningful appeal.
Determinations may not be issued in batches without individual file review; the reviewing physician must document that the member's actual clinical record was examined.

PARTIAL APPROVAL

Dear Member and Treating Clinician:

We have completed a medical-necessity review of the request for 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days for member #88213, who is currently on day 10 of inpatient rehabilitation.

PHYSICIAN REVIEW (Cal. SB 1120): This determination is based on a licensed physician's individualized review of member #88213's clinical record. An automated utilization-review recommendation was not the sole basis for any portion of this decision. The reviewing physician personally examined the attending and physiatrist notes, therapy progress records, and authorization request.

CLINICAL FACTS RELIED ON: Member is age 74, status post hip-fracture open reduction and internal fixation, lives alone with no in-home support, and has two documented falls in the past 12 months. Functional Independence Measure score improved from 68 at admission to 84 by the day-10 review, with documented functional gains each week. The care team documents that discharge to home at day 10 is unsafe without in-home support. The attending physiatrist requested 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days.

GUIDELINE APPLIED: Clinical guideline MSK-04 version 3.0, effective January 5, 2025 (superseding MSK-04 v2.1 in full), is the edition in force on the date of this determination. MSK-04 v2.1 must not be used for determinations on or after that effective date.

COVERAGE DECISION:
- APPROVED: 11 of the 14 requested additional inpatient rehabilitation days (inpatient rehabilitation days 11 through 21, inclusive). Coverage is approved as medically necessary under MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) because the member is age 70 or older, has documented fall risk, has no in-home support, and has documented weekly functional gains during inpatient rehabilitation.
- NOT APPROVED: 3 of the 14 requested additional days (inpatient rehabilitation days 22 through 24). Granting all 14 requested days would result in 24 total inpatient rehabilitation days, exceeding the 21-day maximum in MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) for this clinical profile. The record does not contain additional documented individualized physician justification supporting medical necessity beyond 21 days.

DISCHARGE PLANNING: MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(c) requires a documented home-support plan before discharge when functional-safety thresholds are not yet met. The treating team should coordinate discharge planning and submit updated clinical information if continued inpatient rehabilitation beyond day 21 becomes medically necessary.

APPEAL RIGHTS: You may appeal this determination in writing within 180 days. Include any additional clinical records supporting medical necessity for days beyond 21.

Sincerely,
[Plan Name] Utilization Management

DETERMINATION NOTICE - Prior Authorization PA #88213
Member ID: 88213
Date of Determination: [determination date]

PARTIAL APPROVAL

Dear Member and Treating Clinician:

We have completed a medical-necessity review of the request for 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days for member #88213, who is currently on day 10 of inpatient rehabilitation.

PHYSICIAN REVIEW (Cal. SB 1120): This determination is based on a licensed physician's individualized review of member #88213's clinical record. An automated utilization-review recommendation was not the sole basis for any portion of this decision. The reviewing physician personally examined the attending and physiatrist notes, therapy progress records, and authorization request.

CLINICAL FACTS RELIED ON: Member is age 74, status post hip-fracture open reduction and internal fixation, lives alone with no in-home support, and has two documented falls in the past 12 months. Functional Independence Measure score improved from 68 at admission to 84 by the day-10 review, with documented functional gains each week. The care team documents that discharge to home at day 10 is unsafe without in-home support. The attending physiatrist requested 14 additional inpatient rehabilitation days.

GUIDELINE APPLIED: Clinical guideline MSK-04 version 3.0, effective January 5, 2025 (superseding MSK-04 v2.1 in full), is the edition in force on the date of this determination. MSK-04 v2.1 must not be used for determinations on or after that effective date.

COVERAGE DECISION:
- APPROVED: 11 of the 14 requested additional inpatient rehabilitation days (inpatient rehabilitation days 11 through 21, inclusive). Coverage is approved as medically necessary under MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) because the member is age 70 or older, has documented fall risk, has no in-home support, and has documented weekly functional gains during inpatient rehabilitation.
- NOT APPROVED: 3 of the 14 requested additional days (inpatient rehabilitation days 22 through 24). Granting all 14 requested days would result in 24 total inpatient rehabilitation days, exceeding the 21-day maximum in MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(b) for this clinical profile. The record does not contain additional documented individualized physician justification supporting medical necessity beyond 21 days.

DISCHARGE PLANNING: MSK-04 v3.0 Section 3(c) requires a documented home-support plan before discharge when functional-safety thresholds are not yet met. The treating team should coordinate discharge planning and submit updated clinical information if continued inpatient rehabilitation beyond day 21 becomes medically necessary.

APPEAL RIGHTS: You may appeal this determination in writing within 180 days. Include any additional clinical records supporting medical necessity for days beyond 21.

Sincerely,
[Plan Name] Utilization Management Date of Determination: July 18, 2026. INDIVIDUAL FILE REVIEW ATTESTATION: The licensed physician reviewer confirms that member #88213's actual clinical record for PA #88213 was individually examined and that this determination was not issued from batch processing without per-member file review.
